findings.F1: In agitated bars, an up close is followed by a next-day fall of -0.54 % beyond drift (t -2.23, 1858 cases, 682 days), against -0.04 % in calm bars (t -0.25, 2327 cases); the first up close after a down day carries most of it, at -0.89 % (t -2.70, 1029 cases, 416 days).
findings.F2: Across all agitated days, the next-day excess return falls the higher the close sits in the day's range (coefficient -0.0249 per unit of close location, t -3.58, 3372 cases), and this grows on wider days (close location x log range multiple: -0.0293, t -2.30); a low close on a wide day gives +1.41 % (t 2.24, 302 cases) and a high close on a wide day gives -0.77 % (t -1.59, 297 cases).
findings.F3: Among agitated down days, a fall that is the third close lower in a row is followed by +2.40 % beyond drift (t 2.99, 198 cases, 120 days), against +0.33 % after a first down close (t 1.00, 1024 cases); in calm bars no run length shows anything (t between -0.6 and 0.8).
findings.F4: In agitated markets the range grading is stronger when the fall extends a run: the widest third of down days that follow another down day gives +1.76 % (t 2.40, 266 cases, 134 days), against +0.96 % (t 1.55, 291 cases) for the widest third of first down days, and +0.53 % and +0.19 % for the narrow and middle thirds after a down day.
findings.F5: The tested pattern is concentrated in large, wide agitated falls: the largest-fall third on wide days gives +1.62 % next day (t 2.41, 384 cases), narrow days give -2.84 % (22 cases), and the second day after gives -0.20 % (t -0.31), so the rebound is spent in one day; the same cell in calm bars gives +0.57 % (t 1.52), weaker but not absent (calm down days: log range multiple coefficient 0.0087, t 2.25).
findings.F6: The book earns only on one-day holds: trades held up to 1.5 days average +2.97 % net (927 trades), trades held 1.5 to 2.5 days -2.30 % (365), 2.5 to 4.5 days -5.61 % (186), and over 4.5 days -18.2 % (30). Its gain is skewed: the top 5 % of book days sum to 2.22 times the total and the bottom 5 % to -1.68 times.
findings.F7: In calm bars, a large rise is followed on the second day, not the first, by more rise: the largest-rise third on wide days gives +0.03 % next day (t 0.09) and then +0.75 % the day after (t 2.60, 553 cases); over all calm days, the second-day excess return grows with the day's move in units of usual swing (coefficient 0.0029, t 2.53, 4266 cases).
findings.F8: The angles that showed nothing beyond chance: weekday (the largest of 14 groups has t 2.08, not counted given the number of looks), year (wide agitated falls positive in 2018 to 2021, each t under 1.6), coin (all six positive, t from 1.23 to 2.35), and the 5-day return quintiles (no t above 2.13). The tested idea's per-case move, 0.47 % total and 0.34 % unusual, is 2.4 and 1.7 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, after a coin has closed lower several days in a row, the wider the last day's high-to-low range against its average daily range over the past 30 days, the larger the coin's rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys the rebound mainly when a wide-range fall extends a run of falls, not after an isolated down day.
ideas.name: agitated wide fall-run rebound

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the higher a coin closes within its day's high-to-low range, the lower its return over the next day, and the more so the wider that day's range against its average daily range over the past 30 days.
ideas.consequence: In agitated markets a trader fades strong closes on wide days and buys weak ones, rather than following the day's direction.
ideas.name: agitated close-location next-day reversal

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against its usual daily swing over the past 30 days, the more the coin rises over the following two days, with the rise showing on the second day.
ideas.consequence: In calm markets a trader keeps or adds to a long after a large up day and expects the follow-through a day later.
ideas.name: calm large-rise delayed continuation
